I got four months of "ok" performance from the machine. It leaks if you fill it past half-full of water but the instructions won't mention that. It also does not mention you need to let the unit air dry with the lid open in order to prevent stench and mildew. It cleans with 80-90% effacy if you rinse first AND use Arm and Hammer Super Washing Soda (regular baking soda can work in a pinch). Still, it stopped spinning in 4 months and I wasn't able to wash body towels, bedsheets or comforters in it so this thing made no positive dent in my laundering expenses.

I love this little washing machine. I my apartment is small and I can't have a machine I'm my apartment. I wanted something that I could use to was clothes and maybe not have to go to the laundry so much.
When I use my machine I put it on a folding table near my bathroom sink. You cant use very hot water the instructions say. The sink attachment that is used to put the water in the machine will pop off if the water flow is too high. I've used my shower head to add water. Lol.
I put the clothes in first then add the water.
I use warm water on the hot side but not too hot to mess up the machine. I have wash 2 skirts 3 blouses and maybe a few pieces of underwear in the machine at once and it was good. I use liquid gain like a half cap and a scoop of oxyclean powder. I add the detergent once it is filled. I close the machine and let wash.

The noise level is not so loud, but you can hear it.
I drain my water on a bucket but if you can let it drain down the sink or tub it would perfect.

I add more water and fabric softener next. I allow that to go through a cycle tgen drain that.

Next I take all the clothes out and add the little basket. I can put two blouses in at a time make sure it is even in the basket or else it will knock the machine around.

Over all it is a process but this machine serves its purpose. My clothes comes out clean. I love it.

Additionally, the Keurig machine, after about 10+ uses, stopped recognizing this reusable cup with an error message and would no longer work. There is however a work-around. If you take an IR code from the top of another official Keurig K-carafe cup (the small colorful 1/2" circle on the left side foil top of the K cup) cut it off and tape or glue it to the same location on the reusable cup, my Keurig machine continued to work with this filter. I received this yesterday after looking at it for a few months and finally pulling the trigger and ordering. I was worried it would be too small and not get clothes clean. I have been hand washing my own clothes but now that I am doing my 9 year old grandsons clothes I need to have something more powerful. Last night we put 10 white uniform shirts of his in the machine (think dirty, he's 9). I was surprised at how strong the agitator was and how clean the clothes were. They looked like new. A little bit of lint was on the clothes but once they dried it wiped right off. It took me three spins to spin all the shirts. I hung them to dry on a hanger and he wore one to school this morning. It looked like a brand new shirt. I really did not think the spinner would work that well. The directions that come with it are a bit hard to read (poor translation) but I think I figured it out. I haven't figured out when I would put water in the spinner though, any clues? I wish I would have bought this years ago, no more afternoons at the laundromat, now we can keep up with laundry by doing a bit every night. I have not tried towels yet. I can fit sheets but probably not a blanket.

I just got the washing machine a few hours ago. So far I am impressed for a washer that is only $85. It seems to clean the clothing quite well. However, there are a couple of complaints that I have about the washer though. First off, the water inlet hose is too short and does not fit on any faucet. Because of this, I have to fill the washer using buckets. Usually I pour in three buckets of water, that is enough to get the water to the medium line. Also, the drain hose is gravity based and does not use a pump motor. So a drain that is lower than the washing machine itself will be necessary for draining. I learned the hard way to *never* fill the water to the high line, because the agitator is so strong in the washing machine that the water will actually start spilling over the seams of the doors. So I consider the medium water line to be the maximum amount that I can put in. I am still learning to figure out the proper amount of laundry detergent to put in the washer. It does not take much detergent to end up with excessive suds, so only a tiny amount of detergent is needed with this machine. I also noticed that the machine arrived with damage to the plastic on the spinner side. Luckily though the damage is only cosmetic.

The good and bad side of the machine is that it has some DIY features which give you tons of wiggle room. I set this is up in my bathroom, and use a bowl to manually fill it with water. I try to stay on top of washing my stuff and don't let things pile up because the machine can't handle that much. On average I wash a week's worth of clothes (5 shirts, a sweatshirt, sweatpants, 4 pairs of pants, undergarments) This usually takes 2 loads.
The spin dry portion can't handle too much, so I end up placing no more than 4 pieces of light clothing in there (think 4 t-shirts or 2 pairs of pants, or 1 light sweatshirt). The one time I overloaded the spinner, the plastic lid got sliced off by something. This was totally my fault, and did not break the machine. I use a drop of detergent, and run the machine twice (6 minutes to wash, 2 minutes to rinse). The clothes come out a bit damp or really damp, depending on the material and spin time. I tend to crack open the window overnight, or put the fan on and it tends to dry fairly quickly, so try to do your laundry in the evening.

Life changer for me. I bought this (from another retailer - wanted to be able to use PayPal 6 months no interest, no payments) because I wanted a lightweight portable washer with a gravity drain. A pump (to me) was just another thing that could break and would just make the machine heavier.

Cons:
1). The water intake pipe does not fit any faucet in my home. I tried to find a turkey baster in 4 different stores in town, no luck. I just use a funnel and hold it up to my shower head for ~5 mins to fill for large loads.

2). The power cord is too short. I have to use an outdoor extension cord for it to reach an outlet in my bathroom.

3). Lint trap does almost nothing. Even doing towels, it barely catches any hair or lint.

Pros:
1). Lightweight - very easy for me to lift in and out of my bathtub

2). Quiet - I live in a 2nd floor apartment. To keep it quieter and prevent damage to my tub, I bought some no slip drawer liners and dense scrubby sponges from the Dollar Tree to cushion the "feet". It also prevents the washer from "walking" when the spinner is unbalanced at first from just being loaded. TIP: if you use the water intake to rinse, start rinsing a few seconds BEFORE you turn on the spinner and continue rinsing until the drain water is clear - balances the load much quicker.

3). Cleans very well. Haven't had an issue with clothes not being thoroughly clean after a 6 minut

Perfect for small loads in an apartment with no washer. The main reason I give it 4 stars is that the hose that comes with it does is not compatible with my sink or bathtub faucet. Instead I use a 3 gallon bucket to fill it up with usually about 6-7 gallons of water for a couple pairs of underwear, a shirts and maybe some jean shorts. Still experimenting with load size but it seems perfect for the small loads I need it for.

The instructions are in very broken English (some of it is pretty amusing) but thankfully there are plenty of videos on Youtube by other people that have purchased the washer and demonstrate how to use it.

The washer runs in spurts of about 6 seconds which is a little annoying to listen to, but it's not the worst and doesn't run for long (12 minutes max for one cycle). The spin dryer is practically silent and siphons the water out surprisingly well. I still have to air dry what's left, but that was expected. I've only used it a couple times but so far it was well worth my money to not have to go around the outside of my building and down to the basement to pay for my laundry.
